event.notes: "mode": "auto" means every run resolves this itself — before config.json is even loaded, it asks ESPN for the soonest upcoming card, and if that differs from "name" below it rewrites "name"/"league"/"date", regenerates discovery.title_contains and discovery.search.queries from the new main event's fighters, and clears tracker.picks_videos (a stale roundup URL would just burn a download and a vision pass on the old event's deck). Once this week's card has happened, the next run rolls to whatever's next on its own — no manual retarget. "name"/"league"/"date" below are simply the last-resolved event; edit them by hand only if you delete "mode" and want to pin a specific card again (e.g. a Contender Series week, matched as a substring against ESPN's own event name — punctuation and case ignored, spelling not). "league" pins which scoreboard is searched (ufc / pfl); leave it empty to try UFC then PFL. Add more cards to the top-level "events" array to cover them in the same run — a PFL event the same weekend, say — and the dashboard puts a card selector at the top. If a run logs "No ESPN card found" (or, in auto mode, "No upcoming event found"), something's off with the league or the scoreboard is unreachable — nothing is filtered and off-card fights come back.

sources.title: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Heavyweight main event, moved up after Sean Brady withdrew.
94% of the method votes have this ending by KO either way, and the best method panel agrees unanimously on that — only on who. Cortes-Acosta by KO pays -114 against his -225 moneyline.
The field is 76% Cortes-Acosta but the best predictors are 4 of 7 and the best favorite-pickers are dead even.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Welterweight. One of the host's best bets, though he warns both men have fought rarely and recently enough that there is little to read.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Featherweight prelim headliner; Nakamura won the Road to UFC tournament this year.
The best method predictors were unanimous on a Nakamura KO, but the host never gave the panel's size for this fight, so no method-panel count is recorded.

notes: Women's bantamweight. 91% of the method votes have Milosevic finishing it.
The host said the best method predictors were split between her KO and her submission but gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.

notes: Light heavyweight. The host's second best bet: the best predictors and best favorite-pickers are 100% on Fernando, though the method panel splits evenly between his KO (+155) and his decision (+200).

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Women's strawweight co-main, No. 2 against No. 3. Not one channel picked a KO.
The field is 82% Suarez but the best predictors are only 4 of 7 — the widest field-versus-sharps gap on the card.
The best method predictors were unanimous on Suarez by decision, but the host gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Featherweight, and close everywhere: -116/-103 in odds, 65% Magomedov in the field, and the three sharp panels split between the two men.
FLAG — the host gave this method split without stating its total, so the usual reconciliation check could not run; 45 is the sum of the counts he read out.
The best method panel is split four ways, one vote to each of KO and decision for Delano and KO and submission for Magomedov.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Women's flyweight. Not one channel picked a KO, and the best method predictors go the other way from the field — 2 of 3 have Fernandes by decision.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Middleweight. The host's first best bet: every panel 100% on Kondratavicius and 94% of the method votes a KO, which pays -165 against a -295 moneyline.
The best method predictors were also unanimous on that KO, but the host never gave the panel's size for this fight, so no method-panel count is recorded.

notes: Heavyweight; Lorenco's UFC debut. The field is 56% the debutant while every sharp panel is on Petersen — the host puts that down to Petersen alternating wins and losses.

notes: Flyweight; opens the main card and Degli's UFC debut. The best method predictors are on a submission that only 19% of the field picked, and that the oddsmakers rate behind a decision.

notes: Bantamweight, and a 16-year age gap: Grant is 40, Smith 24.
The host names the lone dissenter across all three sharp panels as Axel MMA, on Grant.
Also one of his best bets, on Smith's moneyline — but note 2 of the 3 best method predictors have the +255 underdog winning.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Welterweight; Ko is the biggest favorite on the card at -705.

FLAG — no moneyline is recorded for this fight. The host said every channel picked Ko but never said how many channels that was, and a headcount nobody stated is not one this engine will invent. Every panel is 100% on Ko, and all 45 method votes are for him, so treat the moneyline as unanimous; the Moneylines tab simply has no count to show.

tally_source.event_name: UFC Fight Night: Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

notes: Featherweight. Calderon took this on four days' notice after Lucas Brennan tore an ACL, so the sample is a third of the card's: 29 channels on the winner, 19 on the method, one best-method predictor, and no method prices posted yet.
The host gave the submission count as "15 out of 90", which cannot be right against a 29-channel field; 19 is what his own split sums to and is used here.
He said the few best predictors who had posted were all on Bashi but gave no panel sizes, so no sharp counts are recorded.
